rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi explains that the earth stirs with vegetation and grows through abundant crop yield.
rows.anchor: اهتزت بالنبات { وربت } بكثرة ريعها عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revived the earth with rain and will likewise revive the dead at the resurrection.
rows.anchor: لمحي الموتى } في الآخرة مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is capable of everything.
rows.anchor: إنه على كل شيء قدير } ظاهر المعنى

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد والسدي
rows.claim: Ilhad means turning away from belief in God's signs; they cannot hide their persons, words, or deeds from Him, a warning to them.
rows.anchor: وهذا وعيد عن قتادة وابن زيد والسدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies their ilhad with the clapping and whistling they practiced.
rows.anchor: إن معنى الإلحاد في آيات الله هو ما كانوا يفعلونه من المكاء والصفير عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they altered God's signs and placed them where they did not belong.
rows.anchor: هو تبديلهم ذلك ووضعه في غير موضعه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators take the signs as proofs of divine unity and ilhad as turning from them and abandoning inference.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين إن المراد بالآيات هنا دلالات التوحيد والإلحاد فيها الانحراف عنها وترك الاستدلال بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes and threatens: the disbeliever and obedient believer are unequal; al-Tabrisi prefers its general application to believer and unbeliever.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن الآية على العموم والمراد بهما المؤمن والكافر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the one cast into the Fire as Abu Jahl and the one safe on Judgment Day as the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima instead identifies the one who comes safe on Judgment Day as Ammar ibn Yasir; al-Tabrisi prefers the general reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو عمار بن ياسر عن عكرمة والصحيح أن الآية على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though phrased as a command, “do as you wish” is a threat, letting each person choose between the two outcomes.
rows.anchor: اعملوا ما شئتم } لفظه لفظ الأمر معناه الوعيد والتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person will not choose the Fire, so must believe in God's signs and not deviate from them.
rows.anchor: فإن العاقل لا يختار الإلقاء في النار فإذا لم يختر ذلك فلا بد أن يؤمن بالآيات فلا يلحد فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people's deeds and none of them is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: إنه بما تعملون } أي بأعمالكم { بصير } عالم لا يخفى عليه شيء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dhikr is the Qur'an, which the disbelievers denied when it came to them.
rows.anchor: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر } الذي هو القرآن وجحدوه { لما جآءهم } أي حين جاءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause leaves the predicate of “those who disbelieved in the Reminder” unstated, with punishment for their disbelief understood.
rows.anchor: ترك خبر إن على تقدير إن الذين كفروا بالذكر يجازون بكفرهم ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala takes “those are called from a distant place” as the predicate of the clause.
rows.anchor: ينادون من مكان بعيد " عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes “it is a mighty Book” the predicate; its pronoun refers to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن قوله { وإنه لكتاب عزيز } في موضع الخبر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation of the Qur'an's might is that no human being can produce anything like it.
rows.anchor: المعنى أن الذكر لكتاب عزيز بأنه لا يقدر أحد من العباد على أن يأتي بمثله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God made it mighty by preserving it from change and substitution.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه عزيز بأعزاز الله عز وجل إياه إذ حفظه من التغيير والتبديل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is also called mighty because God gave it the most complete qualities of sound rulings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عزيز إذ جعله الله على أتم صفات الأحكام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is mighty in that it must be honored by following it and not turning away from it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عزيز بأنه يجب أن يعز ويجل بالانتهاء إلى ما فيه وترك الإعراض عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “mighty” as noble in God's sight.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عزيز أي كريم على الله عز وجل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi say falsehood is Satan, who cannot remove truth from the Qur'an or add falsehood to it.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن الباطل الشيطان ومعناه لا يقدر الشيطان أن ينقص منه حقا أو يزيد فيه باطلا عن قتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: They interpret earlier falsehood as no prior scripture invalidating the Qur'an, and later falsehood as no later book abrogating it.
rows.anchor: وثانيها: أنه لا يأتيه ما يبطله من بين يديه أي من الكتب التي قبله ولا من خلفه أي لا يجيء من بعده كتاب يبطله أي ينسخه عن ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abd Allah says its accounts of the past and future are true and accord with what they report.
rows.anchor: وثالثها: معناه أنه ليس في أخباره عما مضى باطل ولا في أخباره عما يكون في المستقبل باطل بل أخباره كلها موافقة لمخبراتها وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع وأبي عبد الله ع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says falsehood cannot reach the Qur'an from the beginning of its revelation or its end.
rows.anchor: ورابعها: لا يأتيه الباطل من أول تنزيله ولا من آخره عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No falsehood comes from any direction: its wording has no contradiction, its reports no lie, and it is neither opposed, augmented, nor changed; it remains proof until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وخامسها: لا يأتيه الباطل من جهة من الجهات فلا تناقض في ألفاظه ولا كذب في أخباره

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the keys of the heavens and earth as their treasuries.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه خزائن السماوات والأرض عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it according to what He knows benefits His servants.
rows.anchor: أي يوسع الرزق لمن يشاء ويضيق على من يشاء على ما يعلمه من المصالح للعباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything and orders provision according to people's interests.
rows.anchor: إنه بكل شيء عليم } فيفعل ذلك بحسب المصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clarified and laid out the religion of divine unity and disavowal of polytheism, prescribed to Noah and revealed to Muhammad and the other named prophets.
rows.anchor: أي بين لكم ونهج وأوضح من الدين والتوحيد والبراءة من الشرك ما وصى به نوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing religion means adhering to it, acting by its requirements, persisting in it, and calling others to it.
rows.anchor: إقامة الدين التمسك به والعمل بموجبه والدوام عليه والدعاء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told not to disagree in religion, but to unite and agree as God's brothers.
rows.anchor: ولا تتفرقوا أي ولا تختلفوا فيه وائتلفوا فيه واتفقوا وكونوا عباد الله إخوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawhid, sincerity to God, rejecting idols, and leaving ancestral religion weighed heavily on polytheists; they resented Muhammad's selection for revelation and prophethood.
rows.anchor: من توحيد الله والإخلاص له ورفض الأوثان وترك دين الآباء لأنهم قالوا أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Selection is God's, not the polytheists': He chooses a messenger whom He knows can bear the mission, as He chose Muhammad and earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: أي ليس إليهم الاختيار لأن الله يصطفي لرسالته من يشاء على حسب ما يعلم من قيامه بأعباء الرسالة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss is that God selects whichever servants He wills for His religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه الله يصطفي من عباده لدينه من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides to His religion those who turn to obey Him.
rows.anchor: أي ويرشد إلى دينه من يقبل إلى طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of guidance is compared with the statement that those already guided receive further guidance.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God guides to His garden and reward whoever returns to Him with intention and sincerity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يهدي إلى جنته وثوابه من يرجع إليه بالنية والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers disputed only after receiving a way to know the truth of Muhammad's prophethood, then turned away from examining it.
rows.anchor: لم يختلفوا عليك إلا بعد أن أتاهم طريق العلم بصحة نبوتك فعدلوا عن النظر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their motive was injustice, envy, hostility, and eagerness for worldly gain.
rows.anchor: فعلوا ذلك للظلم والحسد والعداوة والحرص على طلب الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they left Muhammad despite knowing he was right, out of envy and fear of losing their leadership.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وما تفرقوا عنه أي عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا بعد أن علموا أنه حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: But for God's prior promise to keep them until an appointed time and delay punishment, He would have judged and punished them immediately.
rows.anchor: ولولا وعد الله تعالى وأخباره بتبقيتهم إلى وقت معلوم وتأخر العذاب عنهم في الحال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God promised to defer their punishment until Judgment Day, when He would destroy the wrongdoer and reward the just.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ولولا وعد الله بتأخير عذابهم إلى يوم القيامة وهو الأجل المسمى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the later inheritors as Jews and Christians, who doubt the Qur'an or Muhammad; their scholars knowingly denied truth while ordinary people doubted it.
rows.anchor: مؤد إلى الريبة عن السدي

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون
rows.claim: Kufans except Asim read the singular “major sin”; the remaining readers use the plural, here and in al-Najm.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم هنا وفي سورة والنجم كبير الإثم على التوحيد والباقون كبائر الإثم على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural is supported by “major sins”; the singular can also denote a collective, as in Qur'anic references to God's blessing and Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: ومن قال كبير فأفرد جاز أن يريد به الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They” may emphasize the subject in “are angry,” with “forgive” as the conditional's answer, or begin a clause whose predicate is “forgive.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هم تأكيدا للضمير في غضبوا ويغفرون جواب إذا ويجوز أن يكون هم ابتداء ويغفرون خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For “they defend themselves,” “they” may modify the preceding accusative, begin a clause, or, per Sibawayh, be raised by an implied verb.
rows.anchor: وكذا هم ينتصرون وإن شئت كان هم وصفا للمنصوب قبله وإن شئت كان مبتدأ وقياس قول سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever wealth people receive is brief worldly enjoyment; they die, and it may be gone before then.
rows.anchor: فهو متاع الحياة الدنيا تتمتعون به أياما ثم تموتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward and bliss, prepared as recompense for obedience, are better and more lasting than small worldly benefits for believers.
rows.anchor: من الثواب والنعيم وما أعده للجزاء على الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust in God means entrusting matters to Him, believing He orders them best, and turning to Him in prayer over whatever befalls.
rows.anchor: والتوكل على الله تفويض الأمور إليه باعتقاد أنها جارية من قبله على أحسن التدبير مع الفزع إليه بالدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who avoid major sins” may be genitive, coordinated with “those who believe,” or nominative as a sentence with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع بالابتداء ويكون الخبر محذوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They avoid major sins and indecencies and forgive wrongs done to themselves when angered.
rows.anchor: والفواحش جمع فاحشة وهي أقبح القبيح والمغفرة في الآية المراد بها ما يتعلق بالإساءة إلى نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam cannot waive God's rights or required punishments and cannot pardon an apostate or comparable offender.
rows.anchor: فأما ما يتعلق بحقوق الله وواجبات حدوده فليس للإمام تركها ولا العفو عنها ولا يجوز له العفو عن المرتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer God by accepting His call in religion and maintain prayer at appointed times and with its conditions.
rows.anchor: أي أجابوه فيما دعاهم إليه من أمور الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shura is mutual deliberation, from the word for consultation, so truth emerges; they do not decide matters individually before consulting others.
rows.anchor: يقال صار هذا الشيء شورى بين القوم إذا تشاوروا فيه وهو فعلي من المشاورة وهي المفاوضة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account identifies them as the Ansar, who gathered and consulted before deciding matters even before Islam and the Prophet's arrival.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المعني بالآية الأنصار كانوا إذا أرادوا أمرا قبل الإسلام وقبل قدوم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Ansar met at Abu Ayyub's house to believe in and support the Prophet after hearing of his appearance and the envoys' arrival; this shows consultation's merit.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك وفي هذا دلالة على فضل المشاورة في الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is consoled: earlier peoples mocked their prophets from ignorance, yet God repeatedly sent proofs and messengers rather than abandon them for mockery.
rows.anchor: الأمم الخالية التي ذكرناها كفرت بالأنبياء وسخرت منهم لفرط جهالتهم وغباوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed earlier peoples with varied punishments despite their greater strength, so Quraysh must not trust its power.
rows.anchor: فأهلكنا من أولئك الأمم بأنواع العذاب من كان أشد قوة ومنعة من قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fate of earlier deniers resembles the fate awaiting Muhammad's people: earlier peoples were destroyed for rejecting messengers, so these people will also be destroyed.
rows.anchor: شبه حال الكفار الماضية بحال هؤلاء في التكذيب ولما أهلك أولئك بتكذيبهم رسلهم فعاقبة هؤلاء أيضا الإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's people must admit that God created the heavens and earth; He is almighty and knows creatures' interests.
rows.anchor: أي لم يكن جوابهم في ذلك إلا أن يقولوا خلقهن يعني السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their admission that God created the heavens and earth exposes their ignorance: they then worship others with Him and deny His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: وهذا إخبار عن غاية جهلهم إذ اعترفوا بأن الله خلق السموات والأرض ثم عبدوا معه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading is mihadan; al-Tabrisi says its explanation was already given in Ta Ha.
rows.anchor: وقرئ مهادا وقد مضى ذكره في طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made paths through the land so people can travel and find their destinations.
rows.anchor: لكي تهتدوا إلى مقاصدكم في أسفاركم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation is that reflecting on the land guides people to religious truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لتهتدوا إلى الحق في الدين بالاعتبار الذي حصل لكم بالنظر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anshara means God brought creatures back to life; al-A'sha's verse about a dead person revived on a woman's breast illustrates “resurrected.”
rows.anchor: أي أحياهم فحيوا قال الأعشى: لو أسندت ميتا إلى نحرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqran means ability or capacity: one says “I could handle this camel” when able to manage it.
rows.anchor: الإقران الإطاقة يقال أقرنت لهذا البعير أي أطقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain in the amount needed, neither excessive nor insufficient; this shows a powerful, choosing agent who measures by wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: بقدر الحاجة لا زائدا عليها فيفسد ولا ناقصا عنها فيضر ولا ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain revives dry land with plants, trees, crops, and fruit; similarly, people will emerge from their graves at resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي جافة يابسة بإخراج النبات والأشجار والزروع والثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of all pairs is male and female animals.
rows.anchor: يعني أزواج الحيوان من ذكر وأنثى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation includes animal and inanimate forms and opposites such as sweet and bitter or wet and dry.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه خلق الأشكال جميعها من الحيوان والجماد فمن الحيوان الذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan lists winter and summer, night and day, sun and moon, heaven and earth, and Paradise and Fire as pairs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأزواج الشتاء والصيف والليل والنهار والشمس والقمر والسماء والأرض والجنة والنار عن الحسن

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies the livestock as camels and cattle, which people ride along with ships.
rows.anchor: والأنعام } من الإبل والبقر عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the livestock meant here to be camels.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإبل { ما تركبون } في البحر والبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that people ride the created conveyances; the pronoun in “their backs” refers to the word “what.”
rows.anchor: فالضمير في ظهوره يعود إلى لفظ ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riders should remember and thank God for subduing their conveyance and declare Him unlike created things.
rows.anchor: فتشكروا على تلك النعمة التي هي تسخير ذلك المركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the vehicle compliant for them, though people could not master it or match it in strength themselves.
rows.anchor: أي مطيقين مقاومين في القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riders also say they return to God at life's end on another conveyance, the funeral bier.
rows.anchor: في آخر عمرنا على مركب آخر وهو الجنازة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God taught people what to say when they ride.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: قد علمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص والباقون وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir and Hafs read “he said,” the rest “say”; Abu Ja'far reads “we brought you,” while the rest have “I brought you.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وحفص قال أولو وقرأ الباقون قل أولو وقرأ أبو جعفر جئناكم والباقون جئتكم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With “he said,” the warner addresses them; with “say,” God instructs the warner to tell them through revelation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: من قرأ قال فالمعنى قال لهم النذير أولو جئتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes their error: did they invent the claim or receive a prior scripture supporting it? “Am” indicates an omitted interrogative hamza.
rows.anchor: وهو استفهام بمعنى التقرير لهم على خطئهم والتقدير أهذا الذي ذكروه شيء تخرصوه وافتعلوه أم آتيناهم كتابا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Suddi gloss ummah as a religion or way.
rows.anchor: أي على ملة وطريقة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i instead explains it as a community united in agreement on their belief.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على جماعة أي كانوا مجتمعين موافقين على ما نحن عليه عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim to be guided by following their ancestors' guidance.
rows.anchor: وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون } نهتدي بهداهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent people who preferred luxury to seeking proof—the leaders—made the ancestral-tradition argument in every town.
rows.anchor: إلا قال مترفوها } وهم المتنعمون الذين آثروا الترفه على طلب الحجة يريد الرؤساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following ancestors without proof is irrational: rival groups inherit conflicting beliefs while each thinks others wrong, so one must use rational or revealed evidence.
rows.anchor: والتقليد قبيح في العقول إذ لو كان جائزا لكان يلزم في ذلك أن يكون الحق في الشيء ونقيضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet invites them gently: if he brought guidance better than their ancestors' way, they should follow it.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا أحسن التلطف في الاستدعاء إلى الحق وهو أنه لو كان ما يدعونه حقا وهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They refused the invitation and declared themselves unbelievers in the messengers' message.
rows.anchor: وقالوا إنا بما أرسلتم به } أيها الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God took vengeance by destroying them and hastening punishment; the example shows the good end belongs to truth and its affirmers.
rows.anchor: بأن أهلكناهم وعجلنا عقوبتهم { فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وابن عامر وحفص والباقون
rows.claim: Medinan readers, Ibn Amir, and Hafs include the pronoun ha in “what souls desire”; the remaining readers omit it.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر وحفص ما تشتهيه الأنفس بزيادة الهاء والباقون تشتهي الأنفس بحذف الهاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says both forms are good, but deletion is preferable because the Qur'an generally omits such relative pronouns.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: حذف هذه الهاء من الصلة في الحسن كإثباتها إلا أن الحذف يرجح على الإثبات

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali also argues by analogy that long nouns can lose letters, supporting deletion of the pronoun.
rows.anchor: ويقوي الحذف من جهة القياس أنه اسم قال طال والأسماء إذا طالت فقد يحذف منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hubur is joy whose trace shows on the face; habartuhu means “I beautified it,” and hibar is a trace.
rows.anchor: الحبور السرور الذي يظهر في الوجه أثره وحبرته أي حسنته والحبار الأثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sihaf are eating dishes; akwab are jug-shaped vessels without handles or spouts, and some say a kub is a drinking cup.
rows.anchor: الصحاف جمع صحفة وهي اللجام الذي يؤكل فيه الطعام والأكواب جمع كوب وهي إناء على صورة الإبريق

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's verse about wine with foam between a kub and a jar illustrates the vessel as a cup.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: صريفية طيب طعمها لها زبد بين كوب ودن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Paradise is given for deeds: the believer inherits the unbeliever's Paradise and the unbeliever inherits the believer's Fire.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الكافر يرث نار المؤمن والمؤمن يرث جنة الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi connects this inheritance language with “those are the inheritors.”
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله أولئك هم الوارثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in Paradise have abundant fruit alongside food and drink, and it all lasts; this fulfills every desire.
rows.anchor: جمع لهم بين الطعام والشراب والفواكه وبين دوام ذلك فهذه غاية الأمنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals remain forever in Hell, and their punishment is never eased.
rows.anchor: دائمون { لا يفتر عنهم } العذاب أي لا يخفف عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They despair of every good.
rows.anchor: وهم فيه مبلسون } آيسون من كل خير

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وابن عامر والباقون
rows.claim: Medinan readers and Ibn Amir read maqam with a damma; the others read it with a fatha.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر في مقام بالضم والباقون في مقام بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fatha means a place of sitting or gathering, supported by the description of security; a damma can mean a place of residence or a verbal noun with “place of” omitted, making both readings similar.
rows.anchor: من فتح الميم أراد به المجلس والمشهد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Sundus is silk and istabraq thick, compact brocade; al-Zajjaj says istabraq is named for its intense sheen.
rows.anchor: السندس الحرير والإستبرق الديباج الغليظ الصفيق قال الزجاج: إنما قيل له استبرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hur is the plural of hawra, denoting intense whiteness and white faces; ayn is the plural of aynaa, large-eyed.
rows.anchor: وهو شدة البياض وهن البيض الوجوه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda defines hawra as an eye with intensely white sclera and intensely black pupil.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة الحوراء الشديدة بياض العين الشديدة سوادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” is a prepositional phrase serving as predicate of an implied subject: “the matter is thus.”
rows.anchor: كذلك جار ومجرور في موضع رفع بأنه خبر المبتدأ التقدير الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Facing one another” is accusative as a circumstantial expression of those wearing garments.
rows.anchor: متقابلين نصب على الحال من يلبسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They wear” may be a second predicate or a circumstantial clause attached to “in a place”; its object of garments is omitted.
rows.anchor: ويلبسون يجوز أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر ويجوز أن يكون حالا من الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Secure” is a circumstantial expression attached to “they call for.”
rows.anchor: فآمنين حال من يدعون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the first death as an exception meaning “other than” the death tasted in this world, comparing it with another Qur'anic exception.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: معناه سوى الموتة التي ذاقوها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi says “other than” is an adverb while illa is a particle; he prefers parsing illa and what follows as an adjective or substitute meaning ghayr, since the first death is past.
rows.anchor: وأقول إن سوى لا يكون إلا ظرفا وإلا حرف فكيف يكون بمعناه فالأولى أن يكون إلا هنا مع ما بعدها صفة أو بدلا بمعنى غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As a favor from your Lord” may state the purpose of God's act, be governed by an implied verb meaning “He gave them,” or confirm what preceded as God's favor.
rows.anchor: مفعول له تقديره فعل الله ذلك بهم فضلا منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the people of Paradise are safe from indigestion, illnesses, and pain.
rows.anchor: وقيل آمنين من التخم والأسقام والأوجاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is likened to unpleasant food that one tastes, then denied for Paradise's people.
rows.anchor: شبه الموت بالطعام الذي يذاق ويتكره عند المذاق ثم نفى أن يكون ذلك في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though all afterlife inhabitants avoid death, this reassurance singles out the blessed to promise pleasant life; those enduring deathlike punishment undergo repeated deaths from torment.
rows.anchor: مع أن جميع أهل الآخرة لا يذوقون الموت لما في ذلك من البشارة لهم بالحياة الهنيئة في الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the exception to mean “after the first death.”
rows.anchor: قيل معناه بعد الموتة الأولى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation means that they have already tasted the first death.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining interpretation means “other than the first death”; al-Tabrisi's grammatical explanation is in the preceding segment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سوى الموتة الأولى وقد بينا ما عندنا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps them away from the punishment of the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي فصرف عنهم عذاب النار

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila argue that a sinful believer cannot leave Hell, since this verse says the saved people are protected from the Fire.
rows.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذا على أن الفاسق الملي لا يخرج من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may concern those who do not deserve entry, those pardoned despite deserving it, or protection forever or from the kind of torment reserved for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن ذلك أن هذه الآية يجوز أن تكون مختصة بمن لا يستحق دخول النار فلا يدخلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their bliss is God's favor: He created and blessed them, gave them reason and signs of His unity and obedience's goodness, then rewarded good deeds tenfold.
rows.anchor: لأنه سبحانه خلقهم وأنعم عليهم وركب فيهم العقل وكلفهم وبين لهم من الآيات ما استدلوا به على وحدانية الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is called favor even if deserved because the conditions creating entitlement—moral responsibility and ability—are themselves God's favor.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما سماه فضلا وإن كان مستحقا لأن سبب الاستحقاق هو التكليف والتمكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is victory in attaining what is sought, a matter of great consequence.
rows.anchor: أي الظفر بالمطلوب العظيم الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Qur'an easy on Muhammad's tongue and its recitation easy for him; the pronoun refers to an unstated Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي سهلنا القرآن فالهاء كناية عن غير مذكور والمعنى هونا القرآن على لسانك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God made the Qur'an Arabic so Muhammad and his people could understand it easily.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه جعلنا القرآن عربيا ليسهل عليك وعلى قومك تفهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is for people to remember the Qur'an's commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats and reflect on them.
rows.anchor: ليتذكروا ما فيه من الأمر والنهي والوعد والوعيد ويتفكروا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away, Muhammad should await God's promise; they count as waiting because the good expect reward and wrongdoers expect consequences.
rows.anchor: فإن أعرضوا ولم يقبلوا فانتظر مجيء ما وعدناك به إنهم منتظرون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other readings tell Muhammad to await God's punishment or victory, while they expect adversity for him or think they will defeat him.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه انتظر بهم عذاب الله فإنهم ينتظرون بك الدوائر

rows.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة
rows.claim: Ali and al-Sulami read atharah with a still th; Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and Qatada are reported with another vocalization; the common reading is itharah with an alif.
rows.anchor: قرأ علي ع وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي أو أثرة بسكون الثاء من غير ألف وقرأ ابن عباس بخلاف وعكرمة وقتادة أو أثرة بفتحتين

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says atharah and itharah mean a remnant or trace, as in transmitted speech, an artifact, or a sword bearing a mark of workmanship; singular atharah is stronger because it asks for even one rare piece of proof.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني: الأثرة والإثارة البقية وهي ما يؤثر من قولهم أثر الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation was not purposeless: God created the heavens and earth to subject their inhabitants to commands, expose them to reward and blessings, and repay their deeds in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: ما خلقناهما عبثا ولا باطلا وإنما خلقناهما لنتعبد سكانهما بالأمر والنهي ونعرضهم للثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term is Judgment Day, whose timing God keeps hidden from people; when it arrives, time ends and resurrection begins.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة فإنه أجل مسمى عنده مطوي عن العباد علمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the term is specified for the angels and recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو مسمى للملائكة وفي اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers turn away from reflecting on the resurrection and recompense they were warned about.
rows.anchor: أي أن الكافرين عما أنذروا من القيامة والجزاء معرضون عادلون عن التفكر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols created nothing on earth to merit worship and gratitude, nor do they share in creating or determining the heavens.
rows.anchor: فاستحقوا بخلق ذلك العبادة والشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are challenged to produce an earlier scripture that supports their claim about idols.
rows.anchor: القرآن أنزله الله يدل على صحة قولكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss is a remnant of knowledge preserved from earlier books that says idols are God's partners.
rows.anchor: أي بقية من علم يؤثر من كتب الأولين يعلمون به أنهم شركاء الله

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil explain it as a report from earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أو أثارة من علم أي خبر من الأنبياء عن عكرمة ومقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as a written line, meaning a written book.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الخط أي بكتاب مكتوب عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it is a particular piece of knowledge reserved for you.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خاصة من علم أوثرتم بها عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge demands one of three proofs: reason, scripture, or transmitted report; lacking all three makes their claim false.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فهاتوا إحدى هذه الحجج الثلاث أولاها دليل العقل والثانية الكتاب والثالثة الخبر المتواتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing is more astray than worshipping beings besides God that never answer or help their callers, even if called until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أي من أضل عن طريق الصواب ممن يدعو من دون الله شيئا لو دعاه إلى يوم القيامة لم يجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings they call on neither know of their prayers nor hear them.
rows.anchor: ومن يدعونهم مع ذلك لا علم لهم بدعائهم ولا يسمعون دعاءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural for idols reflects attributing to them an act associated with rational beings, as in Joseph's description of the stars prostrating.
rows.anchor: رأيتهم لي ساجدين [يوسف: 4]
